    Building the Linux distribution

    Start with the shared build instructions. The supported build baseline is Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 / Python 3.12. The automated command is:

    python3.12 tools/build_desktop.py --headless

    It uses tools/linux-requirements.lock for Python wheels and tools/desktop-inputs.json / tools/compiled_sources.json for native downloads. The readable version list is tools/linux-requirements.txt. The DAETools input is its full Linux release, not the C++ SDK alone. The selected Python's native extensions are installed into the dedicated build environment.

    Native portability

    The runtime contains SUNDIALS 7.5.0, SuiteSparse 7.7.0, SuperLU_MT 4.0.1, OpenBLAS 0.3.30, and Zig 0.16.0. The SUNDIALS build applies a recorded source patch because upstream overwrites the requested CMake install RPATH. Installed libraries use $ORIGIN. Staging rejects absolute search paths, dependencies resolved outside the bundle (except the platform C runtime), and missing libraries. Its smoke check runs without LD_LIBRARY_PATH and with only the bundled compiler on PATH.

    The generated release.json records the actual minimum glibc version required by shipped ELF files. The compiler's gnu.2.35 target alone does not determine the application's minimum OS: Python, Qt and copied system libraries can require a newer glibc. Build on the oldest OS you intend to support. Ubuntu 24.04 builds are not promised to run on Ubuntu 22.04. Supporting an older base requires a matching Python/Qt/dependency environment and clean-machine validation there.

    The Qt X11 plugin is checked before freezing. Its required dependencies must be available to PyInstaller. TIFF is not an application input/output format, so the unused optional Qt TIFF plugin is omitted. The DAETools hook collects only the supported adapters and their dependency closure. A physical daetools/pyDAE directory is included so DAETools can find its configuration on POSIX systems.

    Manual build and diagnostic commands

    After creating an ordinary isolated Python 3.12 venv and installing the pinned requirements and a matching DAETools 2.6.0 wheel, the underlying steps are:

    python tools/build_help.py --check
python tools/build_app_wheels.py --output build/release-linux/application-wheels
python -m pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall build/release-linux/application-wheels/*.whl
python tools/build_compiled_runtime.py --work build/native --prefix build/native-prefix --jobs 4
python -c "from pathlib import Path; from tools.build_compiled_runtime import fetch; print(fetch('zig_linux', Path('build/native')))"
python tools/bundle_compiled.py --compiler build/native/zig_linux-source/zig-x86_64-linux-0.16.0 --runtime build/native-prefix --destination desktop/vendor/compiled
python tools/bundle_graphviz.py --system
python tools/freeze_desktop.py --output dist/linux
xvfb-run -a python tools/check_desktop_release.py --bundle dist/linux/MultiSolid --output build/linux-validation --qt-platform xcb
python tools/package_linux.py --bundle dist/linux/MultiSolid --output dist/linux/releases --validation build/linux-validation/validation.json

    Use new staging and validation destinations; the individual staging tools refuse to overwrite existing bundles. The automated builder manages its own generated staging directories. With custom native bundle paths, pass --compiled-bundle and --graphviz-bundle to the freezer.

    The validator copies the application into a path containing spaces and Unicode, clears developer search paths, runs the frozen application's checks, and verifies that no bundled files changed. Packaging requires this passing record and checks the inventory again. The tar archive preserves permissions and symlinks. Test the extracted archive with the same validator before publishing, including a clean Linux machine or VM and a real graphical desktop.
